drhp.business: DCM Limited operates in two reportable segments: Real Estate, covering development of the Company's land at Bara Hindu Rao/Kishan Ganj, Delhi and at Hisar, Haryana; and Grey Iron Casting, manufacturing castings for the automotive industry (cars, multi-utility vehicles, tractors, light and heavy commercial vehicles and earth-moving equipment) through its Engineering Division at Village Asron, Punjab. The Engineering Division has been under a labour-unrest-related lockout since October 2019 and remains locked out as of this report. Through its wholly-owned subsidiary DCM Infotech Limited, the group also provides IT infrastructure services in networking, analytics, cloud and digital technologies.
drhp.end_markets: Automotive industry (cars, multi-utility vehicles, tractors, light and heavy commercial vehicles, earth-moving equipment)|Real estate — Delhi and Haryana
drhp.expansion: The Company's principal expansion initiative is the development of its 68.35-acre land parcel at Village Bir Hisar, Sector-23, Hisar, Haryana, under a Joint Development Agreement (JDA) signed August 11, 2022 for an affordable residential plotted colony under the Deen Dayal Jan Awas Yojana-2016. A development license (No. 179 of 2022) was received in November 2022 for 67.275 acres, but was suspended by the Haryana Director General, Town and Country Planning in April 2023; the Company issued a notice of forfeiture and termination of the JDA to the Developer on November 1, 2025, and litigation over the project land is pending before the Delhi High Court Division Bench. No new capacity expansion is disclosed for the Grey Iron Casting (Engineering Division), which remains under lockout since October 2019.

litigation.note: Dispute over the Hisar land Joint Development Agreement: the Haryana Director General, Town and Country Planning suspended the Company's development license (No. 179 of 2022) in April 2023; the Company issued a notice of forfeiture and termination of the JDA to the Developer (GCD Prime) on November 1, 2025; the Developer appealed a July 28, 2026 judgment to the Delhi High Court Division Bench, which stayed the judgment's effect on August 12, 2026 pending final adjudication (read in the Directors' Report / MD&A).

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company's principal expansion initiative is the development of its 68.35-acre land parcel at Village Bir Hisar, Sector-23, Hisar, Haryana, under a Joint Development Agreement (JDA) signed August 11, 2022 for an affordable residential plotted colony under the Deen Dayal Jan Awas Yojana-2016. A development license (No. 179 of 2022) was received in November 2022 for 67.275 acres, but was suspended by the Haryana Director General, Town and Country Planning in April 2023; the Company issued a notice of forfeiture and termination of the JDA to the Developer on November 1, 2025, and litigation over the project land is pending before the Delhi High Court Division Bench. No new capacity expansion is disclosed for the Grey Iron Casting (Engineering Division), which remains under lockout since October 2019.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Grey Iron Casting (Engineering) Division at Village Asron, Punjab has been under a labour-unrest-related lockout since October 22, 2019 and remains locked out; the matter is sub-judice before labour authorities, and unpaid workmen dues have accumulated to Rs. 7,964 lakh.
- The Company's development license for its Hisar land JDA was suspended by the Haryana Director General, Town and Country Planning in April 2023 amid a Deputy Commissioner enquiry; the Company issued a JDA termination/forfeiture notice, and litigation is pending before the Delhi High Court Division Bench, creating uncertainty over the project and the Rs. 5,000 lakh advance received from the Developer.
- The auditor's report and note 44 to the financial statements flag a material uncertainty related to going concern, noting current liabilities (including the Rs. 5,000 lakh JDA advance) exceeded current assets by Rs. 508 lakh as at June 30, 2026.
- The Company's principal credit risk exposure arises from trade receivables, which are generally unsecured; amounts more than 180 days past due are carried as still collectible based on historical behaviour rather than security.
- The Group has financial assets and liabilities denominated in USD (trade receivables, cash, payables) and is exposed to INR/USD exchange rate fluctuations, with a 1% currency move affecting profit before tax by about Rs. 20.49 lakh (FY26).
- Of the Company's five subsidiaries, only DCM Infotech Limited is operational; the remaining four subsidiaries remained non-operational during the year, concentrating group operating performance in one subsidiary.
- During FY26 there was a temporary deviation from the prescribed Board composition under SEBI Listing Regulations, though the Company states it took steps to restore compliance.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- DCM Infotech (wholly-owned subsidiary) is focused on strengthening its presence in Agentic AI-based automation solutions, with multiple customer engagements secured across healthcare and financial services in India.
- DCM Infotech is exploring introduction of its automation/AI solutions in the US market while continuing to provide recurring support to existing customers.
- The Company is evaluating and pursuing various options concerning its Engineering Division (casting) business/operations, subject to Board and stakeholder approvals.
- The Holding Company intends to improve liquidity by focusing on and managing its real-estate assets/operations, including sale/disposal of land parcels not currently in use for business operations.
